sixth, Johnny charged him all over the
ring, taking plenty of punches, but
landing a few on his own hook. The
result was that he earned draw In the
sixth and tenth and had an edge in
the seventh and ninth. There were no
knockdowns.

OSLO, Norway, Sept. 3 .U.N.S0.
Wireless contact with the, polar
submarine Nautilus has been re-
established by radio operators at
land and sea stations in the
arctic, according to dispatches
today.


The Pioneer Whaling Company
of Oslo received cable via
Spitsbergen from its cookery on
Bear Island saying the radio
operator there had intercepted a
wireless message from the
Nautilus Tuesday night.


The Nautilus operator said the
submersible on which Sir Hubert
Wilkins and his exploring party
are attempting to reach the
north pole by diving under the
ice cap was experiencing severe
storms north of Bear Island.


Explorers pointed out that it
was nothing for Arctic expedi-
tions to be missing for months,
and radio experts said that prob
ably meteorological phenomena,
such as the aurora borealiS. or
the barrier" which turned back
the Graf Zeppelin's signals, might
have prevented Sir Hubert from
communicating with the outside
world.


Said Captain Nielsen. former
commander of German Uboat:


1.-THE Nautilus is able to stay


under water for four days, but


do not believe she has dived


under the ice. because Of the


damage to her depth rudder."

President Hoover was back at his desk
before 8 o'clock this morning after a
pleasant and restful week end at his
fishing camp in the Blue Ridge Noun
tains.


It was the Presidents intention when
he left the White House early Saturday
for his mountain retreat to remain until
this morning, but developments in
Nicaragua and Honduras are understood
10 have caused him to cut short his stay
and return yesterday after noon.


Finds Traffic Jam.


The ride back was interesting and
ENJOYABLE until the presidential party
ran into traffic jam on the lower
Alexandria road leading into Washing
ton. The Presidents cars entered from
the Columbia Pike. A short distance
farther on the presidential cars, by
careful maneuvering were turned back
and reached the Highway Bridge by the
Military road which skirts the Agrl-
cultural Experiment Station and Airing
ton Cemetery.


When the bridge was reached the
President ran flush into another Snarl.
The principal cause of the bridge con-
gestion was the stalled car of an old
colored man. Secret Service men
pushed the rusty old car for consider
able distance hoping to make SUI
ficient opening for the Presidents party
to get through. When they had &C
complished this after much putting and
pushing the motorist discovered that
the reason his car would not run was
because it was out of gasoline.


He reached into the back OF the car,
where his wife and several small chill
cren were sitting and excitedly offering
him suggestions, and produced gaso-
line can. AS he lifted the potato stop
per the old motorist bowed to President
Hoover, who was looking on good
humoredly from his car close by, and
then poured gasoline into the empty
tank.


Delayed rs Minutes.


This road tie-up caused about IS
minutes delay in the return trip. How
ever, the President reached the White
House about $50 o'clock Mrs. Hoover,
with Allan Hoover, left the camp ahead
of the President, with Allan at the
wheel. They came to Washington by
a different route and met with no traf-
nc difficulties


In the Presidents car on the return
Journey were Associate Justice Stone of
the United States Supreme Court and
Mrs. Stone. Assistant Secretary Of the
Treasury Heath and Assistant Secre-
tary of the Navy Janncke.


Few engagements were made for the
President today. The understanding is
that he Is anxious to occupy himself
principally with the present problems
In Central America.

NEW YORK, September 14-The
stock market finally broke into new
low ground of the bear movement to-
day. Prices were weak all day, but
trading was heaviest in the first hour
and again in the last. Just before the
close there was feeble rally on short
covering, but the list as a whole left
OF not much above the worst


The selling was not eXplainable by
any specific development in the news
Rather it was the result of general
encouragement over the action of the
market and over the business outlook.
Bonds went down with stocks, but COM
modities did better, especially the
grains. There was no hint of anything
unfavorable abroad in the action Of the
foreign exchanges.


Among the stocks receiving better
support than the average at the end
were Delaware g. Hudson among the
rails and General MOTORS among the
industrials, although both of them
made new lows during the day.


Liquidation was In evidence directly
from the start and long list of new
lows was established In both rails and
induStrials. During the first half hour
100000 shares changed hands, the
equivalent of 100000 for a full five
hour session. Volume fell off after the
overnight orders had been executed, but,
even so, 1t was the most active early
trading in long time.


There was no new reason for the
selling. There was still concern about
the foreign situation, but nothing to
indicate that it had changed impor-
family over the week end. The London
market was quiet, but Berlin was weak.
Both sterling and mark exchange were
supported at slightly higher levels than
those on Saturday.


At home the news was negatively
favorable. Commodity prices, when
they were lower. reacted because Of the
weakness in the stock market and not
because Of any new pressure. Never
theless the lack of definite signs of
trade improvement and the fear Of
further dividend reductions and omis-
sions dominated the speculative and
investment mind. The Street was
worrying today about the next dividend
declaration on United States Steel COM
mon. although the 81 declared in july
will not be paid for two weeks yet. The
next meeting is scheduled for the last
Tuesday in October. On Wednesday
next Westinghouse directors will meet
but the Baltimore g. Ohio date has
been postponed. In all these cases the
inclination is TO accept the most pes
Simistic view.


United States Steel's new low under
$79 a share had not been duplicated
since 1921, while Baltimore g. Ohio
around 80 was at the lowest since that
same year. These are two typical cases.
The railroad list OF new lows included
Atchison, Lackawanna, Reading. Unior
Pacific and many others. Among the
industrials the electrical manufactur-
ing shares were heavily sold. both

lakes.

sanctuary and will kill any animal found

PITTSBURGH, August ~. - The
Italian Vice Consulate Building was
badly damaged by a bomb explosion
here early today.


The front porch of the three-story
brick structure. in the fashionable Oak
land residential district, was demol-
ished, plaster was torn loose in several
rooms, furnishings were wrecked and
windows shattered.


The explosion, which was heard in
the downtown district, miles away.

and broke windows.

he knew of no reason for the attack.

telephone rang, but that when he TOOK
the receiver down there was no answer.
Later he heard footsteps on the porch
and then the explosion occurred.


Two automobiles parked across the
street from the consulate building were
overturned by the explosion.


The damaged building was under po-
lice guard today, while detectives
conbed the underworld for clues.

The pale greenery Of early Spring
gives place now TO the richer. ripper
green of late Spring. Already, indeed,
there are signs of full. Summer, when
the foliage. both in country and in city
streets, takes on the dark blue-green
of Summers full resplendency. Now
the last tree has leafed out. Even the
late-comerS. like the oaks and lindens,
the catalpas and the princess tree, have
got under way with their great archi-
tectural task of the year, the construc-
ton and suspension of that complex
breathing organism called the leaf.


On a very large tree, say a giant elm,
there is sometimes almost an acre of
leaf surface (for We must count both
sides of the leaf in calculating the
area and every bit of it. of fine,
sunny day. is hard at work. Leaves
are the lungs. liver and stomach Of a
plant. They are factories that make
no smoke or noise. but on the contrary,
give shade and rustling music, and
diminish the dust and disease of their
neighborhood; and as every school
child knows (and many adults have
forgotten) they give off oxygen, the
gas that animals need, and use the
carbon gas that animals breathe out.


Every school child, too. is asked to
digest the word chlorophyll, which
merely means leat-green. 1t Is word
worth mastering, for we are chloro-
phyllis dependents. The green coloring
matter IN the leaf, with. chemical for
mula almost foot and half long,
bitches up, by some means mysterious,
the energy of the sun and with that
energy makes lifeless water and min
eral salts derived from the soil by the
roots, into simple sugars and starches
Out of these it Celebrates all the other
plant products, and in them one can
swiftly enumerate everything we eat
except meat products, milk products
and eggs; everything we wear. except
silk, WOOL fur and leather; everything
without exception that We burn for
fuel. and, beside construction lumber
fascinating miscellany of products
like tobacco. quinine, camphor, rubber
some dyes, many perfumes and alcohols
tar. pitch, turpentine. the opiates and
cocaine, innumerable cordage fibers
and the many oils and wines.

COLLEGE PARK, Md. June 22.--At-
tanning the highest honor University of
Maryland co-eds can achieve, three
Washington girls and one girl from
Hyattsville have been elected to the
Women's Senior Honor Society.

sal Second street southeast; Miss EloySe
Sargent, 1925 Twenty-sixth street north
east; Miss Rosalie Godhart, 2913 Twen-
tieth street northeast, and Miss Mar
garet Herring of Hyattsville, Md.


Only those junior girls who have made
a "B" or higher average since their
freshman year are eligible to the society,
and not more than Is per cent Of the
class may be admitted. Character.

eligibility.

was elected president of the society for
the coming year. Miss Goodhart was
chosen vice president and Miss Sargent
secretary-treasurer.

markets has widened which ought

mand.

By the Associated Press


PARIS, January 1.-The oficial
French news agency, Havas, issued a
denial this afternoon of a report that
Marshal Joffre had died.


The marshal, who has fought his way
past death through sheer vitality for
the past 10 days, outlived even an APP
parently official report that he had died
at noon today.


The report was flashed across the
world, but few minutes later an official
bulletin issued by his five physicians
said the marshal was still alive, resting
easily although pulse and respiration
were not normal.


False Report Accepted.


The first report of his death, which
had been expected momentarily for the
past week, came little after noon. It
was accepted without question, for the
rugged old hero's amazing vigor had
baff1ed his doctors and they had ex-
pected that he would reach the end of
his resources at any minute.


At little after l o'clock the doctors
issued their official denial that the pa
tent had died.


Premier's Aide Reads Denial.


The secretary to Theodore Steeg,
premier Of France, accompanied by
member of the staff of President
'~Symergue, stood at the top of the hos
pltal steps while the great crowd out
side listened eagerly and read the ON
cial communique denying the report of
the marshal's death.


One Of the holy brothers, speaking
for the father superior of the hospital,
told the Associated Press a few minutes
later that Marshal Joffre was still
alive but in very grave condition.

"many interesting fssure facts have

located before they can cause any dam
age, whereas prior to two years ago
their presence was not known until
they had grown to the surface or
broken the rail" Drake said.

Human beings can be divided into
two fundamental types-the regular
breathers and the irregular breathers.


Such, at least, Is the conclusion of
the British Psychologists F. L. Cola and
S. A. Antonovitch. They determined
the habitual respiration Of their sub
jectS with q plethysmograph, a delicate
instrument used by surgeons, and found
that they fell into two fairly definite
groups. Then they applied various
psychological tests.


They found the irregulars had pre-
dominantly auditory and the regulars
predominantly visual imagery. The reg
ulars had better ears for music and
made better marks in mental arith-
metic. The breathing Of the irregulars
tended to become regular when faced
with problems requiring only visual
imagery. The irregulars were higher
in general ability.


The regulars reported that in their
dreams they only saw things" They
never heard anything. The dreams of
the irregulars were mixed.

ground where the fumes had
settled and then Ieaped into
the air like a great ocean wave.


Men and women became
frantic, screaming and running
blindly through the hell of
flames. Many were hideOuSIy
burned before we could carry

"The oil tanks went fast.

age to get down to Havana, and

Without Mercy


Tony was killing her child.

he came into the nursery to

ing she looked at him coldly,
and said she would stay with
Lael. Her dinner was sent UP

Lael was sick, perhaps dying,

what the doctor had asked.


She touched the baby's hot
still fingers, and a tremor
passed through her body. She
must do something. She could
not sit this way, helpless, in
active when Lael needed care,
had to live.


In the three days she had
been with Tony she had been
a prisoner IN his house. True
she had taken walks around

moments when Lael was asleep.
The servants had been kind,
too kind. One afternoon she

Petty robberies and bold hold-ups

Corp. Paul and Moore sped out along

ped all approaching automobiles.

lice and firemen were deluged with

vicinity. AT the fourth precinct more

There was little or no breeze during

ticularly strong in lox-lying sections of

sentries from their posts at the Army

suspension of work in the gun shops at

respective commanding officers.


The odor Of Illuminating gas. how
ever, was especially strong at the War

iShed around midnight.


Receiving numerous inquiries by tele-
phone early last night, the gas COM

in emergency cars to comb the affected
area for possible leaks in gas mains.
Company officers pointed cut this search
was unavailing last night and this
morning, and expressed the opinion the
fumes were not illuminating gas.


Sewers Investigated.


A report that gas had been dumped
into sewers from the giant reservoir at
Twelfth and NJ streets southeast also
was denied by company officials. They
explained that the purifying agent was
changed at the reservoir days ago and
that some of the waste went into the
sewers at that time. but that this could
no be blamed for any fumes last night.


Heads of the Sewer Department were
investigating to see if the mysterious
gas cloud could be traced to the Dis
tricts sewers, but had found no indi-
cation of this at a late hour today.


An atmospheric condition of almost
absolute calm prevailed over the Dis
trict early last night, the Weather
Bureau said. virtually eliminating the
possibility that the fumes were blown

COLONIAL BEACH, Va, June s.

during an attempted swim to the Vir-

%. His companion, Miss Hilda Nor
rison of Cherrydale, Va, reached the
shore after being in the water for eight
hours.


Identification closes the last chap
ter of one of the most unusual river
stories ever enacted in this section.
hewitt and Miss Morrison had padded
their canoe the seven miles separating
the Virginia and Maryland shores and
were attempting the return trip when
high wind caused their canoe to
overturn. Both chung to poles support
ing a fish net until hopes of rescue
died and then attempted the long swim
to the Virginia shore.


Both we're excellent swimmers, but
Miss Morrison possessed the more
stamina and reached safety after an
eight-hour swim. Nevitt's parents did
not give up hope for him until several
days after the tragedy. believing that
he may have landed at some obscure
spot and would eventually be found
alive
